channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula afirma que Brasil e Portugal vivem melhor momento da relação e exalta brasileiros no país: 'Povo trabalhador'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated during a visit to Portugal that Brazil and the country are experiencing their best bilateral relations ever, praising Brazilians as hardworking, skilled professionals contributing to Portugal’s middle class through home purchases and labor integration. He also criticized global unilateralism and the weakening of the UN, thanked Portugal for supporting the Mercosul-EU agreement, and jokingly said Donald Trump should 'win' the Nobel Peace Prize soon to end world wars.

item.title: Lula põe Trump no colo de Flávio
item.description: Lula stated that a potential interference by Trump in Brazil’s succession would greatly help him, suggesting the former U.S. president could influence the political landscape in his favor. The remark was made shortly before departing for Europe, sparking speculation about external alliances in the 2026 election race.

item.title: Lula diz que é preciso “dar logo” o Nobel da Paz a Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva suggested that the Nobel Peace Prize be awarded immediately to Donald Trump, arguing it would prevent the former U.S. president from initiating further global conflicts. The remark was made during his visit to Lisbon, where he met with Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro, emphasizing the EU-Mercosul agreement and discussing immigration issues affecting Brazilians in Portugal.

item.title: Sátira do Porta dos Fundos contra Gilmar Mendes volta a viralizar
item.description: A 2018 satirical video by Porta dos Fundos resurfaced in April 2026 after Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes filed a crime report against former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema over an episode of Zema's series 'Os Intocáveis'. The video mocks Mendes by likening him to an 'Ipiranga gas station' of the STF, implying he routinely grants favors like habeas corpus to allies. Zema claimed he is being 'persecuted' by the Court, while Mendes' office stated they have no plans to take action against the comedy group.

item.title: Direita portuguesa prepara manifestação para chegada de Lula em Lisboa
item.description: Portuguese right-wing leaders, headed by Chega party president André Ventura, are organizing a protest against the arrival of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Lisbon, scheduled for Tuesday, April 21. The demonstration will take place in front of the Belém Palace, the official residence of the Portuguese president, with Ventura labeling Lula a 'thief' and declaring 'a thief's place is in prison'. Approximately 80,000 eligible Brazilian voters reside in Portugal, 62,000 of them in Lisbon.

item.title: Em Portugal, Lula diz que Trump tem que 'ganhar logo' Nobel da Paz para acabar com as guerras
item.description: During a visit to Portugal, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) joked that Donald Trump should 'win' the Nobel Peace Prize soon to end global wars. He criticized Trump's claims of having ended eight conflicts and defended multilateralism, lamenting the UN's weakened role in mediating wars. Lula stressed his support for international cooperation and criticized unilateralism and protectionism during his European tour.

item.title: Alemanha anuncia investimento de 700 milhões de euros no Brasil em clima e mobilidade verde
item.description: Germany announced an investment of 700 million euros (approximately R$ 4.3 billion) in Brazil for climate and green mobility projects, with 500 million euros allocated to a climate fund and 200 million euros to sustainable mobility initiatives. The commitment was confirmed by BNDES during President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's visit to Hannover and aims to accelerate energy transition, green infrastructure, and carbon emissions reduction, strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two nations.

item.title: Há 1 semana abaixo de R$ 5, real é moeda que mais se valoriza no ano
item.description: The Brazilian real recorded the strongest appreciation against the U.S. dollar among 27 currencies in 2026, gaining 10.4% year-to-date, driven by rising oil and commodity prices and the Central Bank’s restrictive monetary policy, which kept the Selic rate at 15% per annum until March 2026, resulting in high real interest rates. The IMF raised Brazil’s 2026 GDP growth forecast to 1.9%, while foreign investors injected R$67.3 billion into the São Paulo Stock Exchange by April. However, analysts warn that the election year may trigger fiscal pressures that could reverse the currency’s gains.

item.title: O Brasil e o mundo em 2027 (por Marcos Magalhães)
item.description: The article examines the foreign policy visions of the two main pre-candidates in Brazil's 2026 presidential election: Flávio Bolsonaro, who advocates for strategic alignment with the United States and criticizes the Lula government as allegedly anti-American and pro-China, and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who — although the excerpt is incomplete — is portrayed as favoring a more independent and multipolar stance. It emphasizes that the 2026 electoral choices will shape Brazil’s international role in 2027, amid global crises such as wars, climate change, and supply chain disruptions.

item.title: Por que governança é tratada como política de governo e não de Estado?
item.description: Governance fails in Brazil because it is treated as government policy — temporary and partisan — rather than state policy, which is continuous and institutional. This creates misalignment between agents (officials) and principals (society), leading to information asymmetry, distorted incentives, and loss of efficiency and legitimacy. The Banco Master case shows these failures extend beyond the public sector, affecting private organizations and their interactions with the state.

item.title: Gleisi chama Caiado, Tarcísio e Bolsonaros de “traidores da pátria”
item.description: Federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT-PR) accused Ronaldo Caiado (PSD-GO), Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos-SP) and the Bolsonaro family of being "traitors of the homeland" for supporting tariff increases and advocating for foreign exploitation of Brazil's rare earths. In an X post on Tiradentes Day, she said President Lula is defending national sovereignty by strengthening Petrobrás, the BNDES, and PIX, and that the true homage to Tiradentes is protecting Brazil's natural and technological heritage.

item.title: Lula ameça adotar 'reciprocidade' após EUA pedirem saída de delegado da PF envolvido em caso Ramagem
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil may adopt 'reciprocity' measures after the U.S. government requested the removal of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, who served as a liaison officer in Miami. The U.S. request followed the detention of former congressman Alexandre Ramagem on U.S. soil, which U.S. authorities labeled an attempt to manipulate the immigration system. Lula criticized the U.S. action as an abuse of authority and foreign interference, asserting Brazil will not accept such conduct without response.

item.title: Lula chega a Lisboa para debater xenofobia contra brasileiros e aperto na imigração
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva arrived in Lisbon to discuss xenophobia against Brazilians and Portugal’s tightening immigration rules. In a joint statement with Prime Minister Luís Montenegro, Lula mocked Donald Trump and advocated for reforms to the UN Security Council’s statute to reduce global conflicts. The Brazilian government reiterated its interest in cooperating with Portugal to combat xenophobia and ensure legal security for Brazilians amid changes to Portuguese immigration laws.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil pode adotar reciprocidade após EUA expulsar delegado da PF
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said Brazil may adopt reciprocity measures following the expulsion of a Federal Police attaché by the U.S. government. He criticized the U.S. decision as inappropriate and emphasized that Brazil will not tolerate affronts to its sovereignty.

item.title: Lula chama conflito no Oriente Médio de “guerra da insensatez”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva labeled the Middle East conflict a "war of insensibility," criticating the renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran and arguing that the issue could have been resolved by the 2010 Brazil-Turkey-Iran agreement, which the U.S. and EU rejected. He warned that the burden of this conflict will fall on ordinary citizens, particularly truck drivers and consumers of basic goods, due to rising fuel and food prices.

item.title: ‘Se houve abuso, vamos fazer reciprocidade’, diz Lula sobre delegado da PF expulso dos EUA
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil may take reciprocal measures against U.S. police officers in response to the expulsion of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho from the United States. He said Brazil will not accept American abuse or interference in its immigration system, after the U.S. government accused the delegate of manipulating immigration procedures to facilitate the arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramage.

item.title: Lula fala em reciprocidade após expulsão de delegado dos EUA
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated Brazil will reciprocate after the U.S. government requested the departure of a Federal Police delegate involved in the arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem. He said Brazil will not accept interference or abuse of authority by American officials. The U.S. action followed the delegate's attempt to bypass formal legal cooperation mechanisms regarding Ramagem's extradition, a former Abin director who fled to the U.S. after being sentenced to 16 years for a coup plot.

item.title: A questão-chave é a democracia
item.description: The article criticizes Flávio Bolsonaro for overlooking the democratic risk posed by his candidacy, given his support for his father, convicted of attempting a coup, and his promise to pardon him and amnesty others involved. The author argues that focusing on fiscal plans is irrelevant compared to the authoritarian threat he embodies. The central issue is not economic policy, but the survival of Brazilian democracy under a potential second Bolsonaro government.

item.title: Entre a TerraBrás e as mineradoras estrangeiras
item.description: Brazil is experiencing a conflict over control of its critical minerals, with the PT advocating for greater state participation through a production sharing regime, while the Chamber of Deputies advances a bill offering fiscal incentives to private mining companies. The acquisition of Serra Verde, the largest rare earths mine outside Asia, by an American company intensifies the debate, especially after Lula’s statements rejecting the role of mere commodity exporter. The Chamber president included Zé Silva’s bill on the agenda for a vote on April 22.

item.title: Oposição articula impeachment de Gilmar após pedido de investigação contra Zema
item.description: Opposition lawmakers in the Chamber of Deputados announced an impeachment petition against Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, led by Deputy Gilberto Silva (PL-PA), after Mendes requested an investigation into former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) for sharing a satirical video mocking justices. The opposition argues that investigating Zema, a presidential pre-candidate, would set a dangerous precedent by treating institutional criticism as a criminal offense. The petition requires Senate president approval to proceed, as required by the Brazilian Constitution for impeaching Supreme Court justices.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 21 de abril
item.description: The JCaesar cartoon published on April 21, 2026, satirizes the Brazilian political landscape, focusing on figures such as Alexandre de Moraes, Gilmar Mendes, Romeu Zema, and themes like plea bargains, fake news, and the STF. The critical humor reflects institutional tensions and polarization around the judiciary and media, typical of the pre-election climate in 2026.

item.title: Lula fala em revidar após EUA expulsarem delegado da PF
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil may respond with reciprocity if there was abuse of authority by the United States in the expulsion of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo Carvalho, who was stationed in Miami and removed after allegedly monitoring former congressman Alexandre Ramagem in Florida. Lula said he does not accept foreign interference and that Brazil will act firmly, but seeks to ensure things happen correctly. The expulsion followed Ramage’s arrest by ICE, and Carvalho had been involved in international security cooperation since 2023.

item.title: Crise de confiança provoca debate eleitoral sobre reforma do Judiciário
item.description: Judicial reform has become a central theme in Brazil's 2026 electoral campaign, driven by a growing crisis of public trust in the judiciary. Lula and the Workers' Party (PT) propose reforms including redefining the Supreme Federal Tribunal's (STF) responsibilities, establishing judicial conduct rules, combating impunity in serious crimes, and cutting expenditures. Meanwhile, Justice Flávio Dino of the PSB has released a draft proposing additional restrictions on access to superior courts, anti-fraud measures for precatórios, specialized tribunals for specific crimes, and harsher penalties for corruption involving judicial officials.

item.title: Lula promete “reciprocidade” por policial expulso dos EUA
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva commented on the expulsion of a Brazilian police officer from the United States following the release of former Abin director Alexandre Ramagem, stating that 'no foreigner can manipulate our' and promising 'reciprocity' in diplomatic treatment.

item.title: Lula fala em 'reciprocidade' após delegado da PF ser expulso dos EUA
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he may act with 'reciprocity' against the United States following the expulsion of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo by U.S. authorities. Lula stated he was informed of the incident on Tuesday morning, March 21, during a press briefing in Hannover, Germany. The remark comes amid rising diplomatic tensions between the two nations.

item.title: PDT aciona STF e tenta anular eleição na Alerj
item.description: The PDT filed an ADPF with the Supreme Federal Court to annul the election of Douglas Ruas (PL) as president of the Alerj, arguing that the open vote violated constitutional principles such as legislative autonomy and administrative morality. The party demands a new election by secret ballot, the nullification of the April 17 vote, and Ruas’s removal, along with a ruling declaring open voting in the legislature’s leadership election unconstitutional.

item.title: Fachin elogia proposta de Dino para reforma do Judiciário
item.description: Supreme Federal Court President Edson Fachin praised the judicial reform proposal by Minister Flávio Dino, highlighting its structural nature, emphasis on institutional responsibility, and balance between judicial independence and oversight. Fachin stated the debate deserves 'applause and support' and contributes to qualifying public discourse on the Judiciary as a continuous and plural process.

item.title: Na Alemanha, Lula fala de abuso contra policial brasileiro nos EUA
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated in Hannover, Germany, that the Brazilian government may take action against American police if abuse against Marcelo Ivo, a Federal Police attaché in Miami under U.S. investigation, is proven. The remarks were made on Tuesday, April 21, 2026, amid diplomatic tensions over the conduct of Brazilian agents abroad.

item.title: Jogos de hoje, terça, 21 de abril: onde assistir futebol ao vivo e horários
item.description: On Tuesday, April 21, 2026, a busy football schedule features matches from the AFC Champions League, La Liga, Premier League, Copa do Brasil, and national competitions such as the Brasileirão Feminino. Match times range from 1:15 PM to 9:30 PM, broadcast on ESPN, Disney+, SporTV, Amazon Prime Video, and streaming platforms. Notable fixtures include the Brasileirão Feminino games (Fluminense vs. Palmeiras at 4:00 PM and Cruzeiro vs. Internacional at 7:00 PM) and Copa do Brasil matches at 5:00 PM, 7:15 PM, 7:30 PM, and 9:30 PM.

item.title: Lula ameaça reciprocidade contra os EUA no caso de delegado brasileiro envolvido na prisão de Ramagem
item.description: President Lula said he was informed on Tuesday morning (21) about the case of a Brazilian delegate involved in the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem in the U.S., and that if there was abuse by the U.S. government, there will be reciprocity. He stated he does not know the details of the incident. Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira said the news lacks foundation and that Brazil is awaiting clarification from U.S. authorities.

item.title: Presidente da UNE admite desconexão de Lula com jovem: ‘Falta se conectar ao que as pessoas querem’
item.description: UNE president Bianca Borges says Lula's government is disconnected from youth despite advances in health and education, as everyday frustrations like inability to replace phones undermine satisfaction. She argues the 2026 election will be strongly shaped by generational factors and laments youth's disconnection from national history, which benefits conservative discourse. Borges contrasts Lula's lack of a cellphone with Nikolas Ferreira's active social media presence as emblematic of the communication gap.

item.title: Lula diz que pode adotar reciprocidade contra os EUA no caso de delegado envolvido na prisão de Ramagem
item.description: President Lula said he may adopt reciprocity against the U.S. over the case of Brazilian Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, who was ordered to leave the U.S. after being accused of trying to circumvent formal extradition requests for political persecution. Lula stated he will not accept 'American interference and abuse of authority,' while Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira said the report lacks foundation and that they are awaiting clarifications from U.S. authorities. The PF director confirmed Carvalho had been working in Miami with ICE for over two years.

item.title: Contrastes
item.description: President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the frontrunners in polls for the 2026 presidency, display contrasting campaign styles. Lula, leveraging his office, speaks extensively and uses his public image, while Flávio avoids exposure, stays within his comfort zone, and emphasizes the age contrast between himself (44) and Lula (80), despite the latter's visible physical vigor on social media.

item.title: Governo federal diz que continuará adotando medidas para aumentar arrecadação e cumprir metas fiscais
item.description: The federal government submitted the 2027 Budget Guidelines Law (PLDO) to Congress, targeting a primary surplus of 0.5% of GDP (R$ 73.2 billion) for 2027, following projected deficits in Lula’s first three years. Measures include enhancing tax progressivity, reviewing fiscal incentives, and sustaining revenue recovery actions to stabilize public debt over the medium term.

item.title: Master: Aliados veem grupo de Gilmar e Moraes em negação na crise do STF
item.description: Allies of Ministers Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes warn of a possible 'own goal' in the offensive against Senator Alessandro Vieira and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema, who are criticizing the STF over its ties to Banco Master. They fear the attacks could backfire, leading to retaliation or damaging the Court's image. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Brasileira revela xenofobia em demissão de serviço público de Portugal e apela a Lula
item.description: Brazilian Priscila Brandão Gomes, a teacher and operational assistant at the Polytechnic Institute of Lisbon, denounced institutional xenophobia, coercion, and unfair dismissal during her probation period in Portugal, stating her supervisor discriminated against her for being Brazilian. She filed complaints with Lisbon’s Public Prosecutor’s Office and the Commission for Equality and Against Racial Discrimination (CICDR), emphasizing that losing her job threatens her son’s legal residency and his scheduled family reunification interview on May 27. The complaint coincides with President Lula’s visit to Portugal, which includes an agenda to combat xenophobia.

item.title: Brasil tenta emplacar fim da escala 6x1 desde os anos 1980
item.description: The Lula government has sent a bill to Congress to reduce the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, establishing a 5x2 schedule without salary cuts. This proposal, distinct from Erika Hilton’s 36-hour plan, seeks a compromise and revives a debate dating back to the 1980s, when a 40-hour week was approved in a constituent assembly committee. The push originated in the early 1980s labor movement, led by groups like the ABC Paulista metalworkers, opposing the 48-hour week entrenched by the 1943 CLT.

item.title: Início da Copa do Brasil para os principais clubes do país acirra de vez a maratona do calendário em 2026
item.description: The 2026 Copa do Brasil has entered its decisive phase, intensifying an already congested calendar for Brazil’s top clubs, now juggling three simultaneous fronts: Libertadores, Brasileirão, and Copa do Brasil. Flamengo, under Leonardo Jardim, has implemented squad rotation to maintain physical intensity, treating all three competitions as priorities despite previously focusing on Libertadores and Brasileirão in 2025. Physical strain on players is viewed as nearly insurmountable due to the condensed schedule, particularly following the shortened preseason imposed by the new CBF calendar.

item.title: CVM não pode ser moeda de troca em negociação política
item.description: The CVM, which oversees Brazil's R$ 18 trillion capital market, has been without a president for nine months and operates with a reduced board, leading to fewer penalties for irregularities. President Lula's appointment of lawyer Otto Lobo to lead the agency, made early this year, is seen as a political gesture to ease tensions with the Senate, though his confirmation hearing has not yet taken place. Lobo has a record of controversial decisions, including a vote in favor of Banco Master in the Ambipar case, contrary to technical opinions.

item.title: Flávio convida jovens de 16 anos a tirar título de eleitor
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) invited 16-year-olds to obtain their voter registration, stressing the importance of youth participation in the 2026 elections. He criticized the Lula government, accusing it of failing to keep promises and 'stealing the future' of young people, and emphasized the need for change in education, employment, and security.

item.title: Caiado diverge de pré-candidatos de direita e diz apoiar 100% projeto sobre misoginia
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado of the PSD declared full support for the bill criminalizing misogyny, approved by the Federal Senate in April 2026 and currently under debate in the Chamber of Deputies. This stance puts him at odds with other right-wing pre-candidates, who typically oppose such measures. Caiado aims to position himself as a moderate and progressive figure on human rights issues.

item.title: Milei é mal avaliado por 59,7% dos argentinos, diz pesquisa
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei has a 59.7% disapproval rating and 36.2% approval, ranking 14th among 18 Latin American presidents in a CB Global Data survey. Brazil's Lula ranks 7th with 48.4% positive and 49.1% negative evaluations. El Salvador's Nayib Bukele tops the list with 70.1% approval.

item.title: Chefe da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro critica proposta de Dino para o STF, e Gleisi elogia
item.description: The head of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign criticized Flávio Dino's proposal for a judicial reform at the STF, calling it inadequate. In contrast, PT president Gleisi Hoffmann praised Dino's initiative, emphasizing its importance for strengthening institutional integrity.

item.title: O que prevê acordo entre Brasil e Alemanha sobre minerais críticos e terras raras
item.description: Brazil and Germany signed a joint declaration of intent to expand cooperation on critical minerals and rare earths, focusing on research, development, and innovation across the supply chain. The agreement aims to add value to Brazil’s exports by attracting processing and industrial activities domestically, avoiding reliance on raw material exports alone. Lula emphasized Brazil’s goal to be a strategic actor in the global energy transition, not merely a commodity exporter.

item.title: Oposição articula impeachment de Gilmar Mendes após ministro pedir para STF investigar Romeu Zema
item.description: Opposition lawmakers in the Chamber of Deputies announced an impeachment petition against Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes after he requested that former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema be included in the fake news investigation. Led by Deputy Gilberto Silva (PL-PA), the opposition argues the move sets a dangerous precedent by treating institutional criticism as a prosecutable offense, threatening free speech. Zema’s satirical video, depicting puppet versions of Justices Toffoli and Mendes, is framed as legitimate critique of Mendes’ prior ruling annulling data seizures in Toffoli’s company, which received investments from a fund linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: “Não toleram mais qualquer tipo de piada”, diz Zema sobre STF
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential pre-candidate from the Novo party, accused the STF of persecution after a fake news investigation was opened against him over a satirical video titled 'Os Intocáveis', which uses puppets to criticize the STF's ties to Banco Master. He called the investigation a 'free pass' for ministers to act without accountability and argued that by prosecuting satire, they prove they are the untouchables they claim to criticize. Zema defended free speech, quoting George Orwell, and lamented that Brazil is 'declining' by failing to protect the right to criticize those in power.

item.title: Deputados do PDT acionam STF para anular eleição de Douglas Ruas como presidente da Alerj
item.description: State deputies from the PDT filed an action with the STF to annul the election of Douglas Ruas (PL) as president of the Alerj, arguing that the vote was open rather than secret and that the presidency of the Assembly should not be decided until the STF rules on how the interim governor of Rio de Janeiro will be chosen, given the current institutional vacuum. They demand a new secret-ballot vote to prevent interference and ensure legitimacy.

item.title: Governo alemão usa ‘Show das Poderosas’, da Anitta, em post sobre ida de Lula ao País
item.description: Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development used Anitta's hit 'Show das Poderosas' as the soundtrack for an Instagram post celebrating 60 years of Brazil-Germany cooperation and Lula's visit. The post highlights agreements on climate, sustainable mobility, and Amazon preservation, reinforcing a shared commitment to multilateralism amid global tensions. The unconventional music choice surprised social media users, sparking memes and Brazilian users tagging Anitta in the comments.

item.title: PDT recorre ao STF contra eleição na Alerj
item.description: The PDT filed an ADPF with the Brazilian Supreme Court to nullify the election that made Douglas Ruas (PL) president of the Alerj, claiming procedural irregularities and requesting a new vote with secret ballot.

item.title: Aliados de Ramagem comemoram expulsão de delegado da PF pelos EUA
item.description: Allies of Alexandre Ramagem celebrate the expulsion of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo by the United States, after he was accused of attempting to manipulate the U.S. immigration system during Ramagem’s arrest in April 2026. Eduardo Bolsonaro and Paulo Figueiredo claim the move was a response to alleged political persecution, while critics like Marcel Van Hattem and Ludmila Lins Grilo call it a national embarrassment. Ramagem was released on April 15 after being detained by ICE.
